title: Keyturn Roadside Assistance: Lapse and Reinstatement Terms by Plan
content:
## Three figures govern a Keyturn Roadside Assistance subscription whose fee has gone unpaid

The lapse period is the number of calendar days an unpaid fee may stand before cover falls away. The
reinstatement window is the number of calendar days after a lapse within which cover may be restored.
The reinstatement fee is the amount charged to restore lapsed cover.

| Plan | An unpaid fee may stand for (calendar days) | Window after a lapse within which cover may be restored (calendar days) | Fee to restore lapsed cover (USD) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Keyturn Roadside Basic Cover | 30 | 30 | 15.00 |
| Keyturn Roadside Plus Cover | 30 | 45 | 15.00 |
| Keyturn Roadside Tow Cover | 45 | 45 | 20.00 |
| Keyturn Roadside EV Cover | 45 | 45 | 20.00 |
| Keyturn Roadside Fleet Cover | 60 | 60 | 25.00 |
| Keyturn Roadside Concierge Cover | 60 | 90 | 45.00 |

### Notes on the figures

1. The lapse period and the reinstatement window are the same length on Keyturn Roadside Basic Cover
   at 30 calendar days, on Keyturn Roadside Tow Cover and Keyturn Roadside EV Cover at 45, and on
   Keyturn Roadside Fleet Cover at 60. They differ on Keyturn Roadside Plus Cover, where an unpaid fee
   may stand 30 calendar days against a reinstatement window of 45, and on Keyturn Roadside Concierge
   Cover, where the figures are 60 and 90.
2. The reinstatement fee stands at USD 15.00 on Keyturn Roadside Basic Cover and Keyturn Roadside
   Plus Cover, USD 20.00 on Keyturn Roadside Tow Cover and Keyturn Roadside EV Cover, USD 25.00 on
   Keyturn Roadside Fleet Cover and USD 45.00 on Keyturn Roadside Concierge Cover.
